cases.name: silence
cases.what: a dead room: no baseline, so nothing to report

cases.name: one-laugh
cases.what: a two-second laugh over room tone

cases.name: two-laughs
cases.what: two laughs with the room settling between them

cases.name: laugh-at-the-tail
cases.what: still laughing when the recording stops

cases.name: shout-too-short
cases.what: one loud moment below the minimum duration: a dropped glass, not a laugh

cases.name: just-over-threshold
cases.what: the room 2.6x its own baseline: a laugh, but only just — a detector calibrated a notch either way disagrees here

cases.name: threshold-boundary-frame
cases.what: the room nominally exactly 2.5x its baseline: the event starts a frame late, because the frame straddling the transition averages both sides. Which way the comparison itself rounds is unobservable — no float ever lands exactly on the threshold

cases.name: just-under-threshold
cases.what: the room 2.4x its baseline: not a laugh, by the same narrow margin

cases.name: just-over-minimum-duration
cases.what: a reaction one frame longer than the minimum: the shortest thing that counts

cases.name: just-under-minimum-duration
cases.what: the same reaction one frame shorter: nothing to report

cases.name: rising-room
cases.what: a room that gets louder through the set without ever reacting
